angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 317,935 km at 9.42 pc = 0.45 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 106.1727 +/- 0.0141 mas (same row, RUWE 0.97): 9.42 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.457 +/- 0.015 solar radii from Lee et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of GJ 367 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260618355L/abstract): 317,935 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.451 +/- 0.019 solar masses from Lee et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of GJ 367 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260618355L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3535 +/- 127 K from Lee et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of GJ 367 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260618355L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Lee et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of GJ 367 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260618355L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/gj-367.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.772, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
